## Motivation

On gfx950, Kimi-K3 TP8 runs 12-head FP8 MLA zero-padded to 16 heads. items.author: AndreasKaratzas

- `registry.py`: cap the SmolVLM HF reference at `transformers<=5.19` with an `hf` reason, so `test_common.py` skips the HF-vs-vLLM comparison while vLLM-side tests keep running.

## Motivation

The forward hooks page says hooks are attached in `ModelRunner.initialize` and "run on every forward pass". That's not what happens. Hooks are registered **after** CUDA graph capture (`finalize_cuda_graph_capture`), and CUDA graph replay never runs Python hooks. ## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` emits a `block_size=0` placeholder `BlockStored` for every group that has a load window. `MambaSpec` groups get a one-chunk window because they depend on a single state, not because their hashes are meaningless: the offloaded chunk is the recurrent state checkpoint at the chunk's last hash. ## Motivation

With MTP, GLM-5.2 runs the gfx950 DSA indexer logits kernel (`logits_hist`, node 3 of the fused decode indexer) once per verify step on each of its 21 "full" indexer layers. Each request contributes 6 rows (the draft positions), and all 6 rows read the same KV pages, but `logits_hist_m` loads every page once per row. At small batches with long contexts the kernel is bound by those loads.

## Modifications

- **`paged_mqa_logits.cuh`** adds `logits_hist_slot`. `logits_hist_m` is unchanged; its machine code is identical to main's.
  - The new kernel takes rows in slots of 3

items.author: zhentaocc
items.summary: The aiter versions that vLLM pins today (v0.1.25, and also v0.1.26) have the same code. That kernel uses 32-bit buffer loads when. [Discussion: CC @hongxiayang @tjtanaa @vllmellm @giuseppegrossi for ROCm-related issue]
items.body:
### Your current environment

MI355X (gfx950), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0cbac6cd1` (vLLM 0.30.1rc1.dev558, aiter 0.1.23). The aiter versions that vLLM pins today (v0.1.25, and also v0.1.26) have the same code.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` gives wrong attention output on gfx950 when a layer's KV cache is 2–4 GiB. No error is raised.

**Cause.** On gfx950, aiter's `unified_attention` runs `_unified_attention_gfx950`. That kernel uses 32-bit buffer loads when `k.nelement() * k.element_size() <= 2**31 - 1`. vLLM passes K and V as strided views of one cache
discussion: CC @hongxiayang @tjtanaa @vllmellm @giuseppegrossi for ROCm-related issue

items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Fixes MMU fault in DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder tail graphs by keeping a single growing padded query buffer in attention metadata instead of freeing/replacing per-bucket buffers under larger captured ones.
items.body:
- With attention TP > 1 and a FlashMLA backend that pads the query to 64 heads (not `trtllm`, not `flashmla_mega`), DeepSeek-V4.1 caches the zeroed padded query buffer on the step's attention metadata (`q_pad_buffer`) and replaced it whenever the shape changed.
- A decoder tail graph step captures every row bucket on that one metadata, largest first. items.body:
## Overview

`context_attention_fwd` in `prefix_prefill.py` runs `ROCM_ATTN`'s prefills and spec-decode verifies. It gets much slower when a long prefill shares a batch with short requests, which is the normal mixed step of chunked prefill. This PR fixes two causes:

1. **Grid order.** The grid was `(batch, head, query_block)`, with the batch on the fastest axis. MI300/MI355 deal workgroups round-robin over 8 XCDs. The programs of one request have linear ids `i, i + b, i + 2b, ...` for batch size `b`, so with even `b` they reach only some of the XCDs. Decodes (`query_len == 1`) return at once,

### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

items.body:
## Overview

Raise the bar for tests written by coding agents. Adds a 31-line `tests/AGENTS.md` with five rules that change what agents actually do, links it from `AGENTS.md` and `pr-checklist` §2.1, and rewrites the "unit over integration over e2e" line in `AGENTS.md`:

- **User-visible fixes need a real-path test** through `LLM`/`vllm_runner` or `RemoteOpenAIServer`, not only a unit test on hand-built inputs.
- **Show the failure before the fix**: run the new test on the base commit and paste the failing and passing output.
- **Never buy a green CI**: no reruns, retry loops, wider tolerances

The router does not expose the engine's `/abort_request` endpoint, so clients cannot cancel an in-flight request through the router.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Give float32 Triton attention and fused MoE float32 accuracy
items.author: ejrtks1020
items.summary: Changes Triton unified attention and fused-MoE kernels from TF32 to float32 via tf32x3 input precision, matching torch float32 matmul accuracy without affecting fp16/bf16/fp8 paths.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #62582. The Triton unified attention (`TRITON_ATTN`), prefill attention and fused-MoE kernels run float32 `tl.dot` in TF32 on NVIDIA. This PR gives them float32 accuracy by default (3xTF32 on CUDA), matching the PyTorch float32 matmuls in vLLM.

## Claims

- With float32 operands, the three kernels match a float64 reference to float32 accuracy (6–7e-6 relative to output RMS, the same as torch float32) instead of TF32 accuracy (~1.6e-2).

items.title: [Perf][Sampler] Split the full-vocab passes of the Triton top-k/top-p kernel over several programs per row
items.author: kimseunghyun-kr
items.summary: With an active top-k, runs one program per row, and that program sweeps the whole vocab twice: once to gather outliers and once to apply the final mask. On A100 with a 248K vocab, one row takes about 360 µs of GPU time, and most of it is spent in those two swe…
items.body:
## Overview

With an active top-k, `_topk_topp_kernel` runs **one program per row**, and that program sweeps the whole vocab twice: once to gather outliers and once to apply the final mask. On A100 with a 248K vocab, one row takes about 360 µs of GPU time, and most of it is spent in those two sweeps. This PR splits the two sweeps over several programs per row. The pivot search and the top-p search stay as they are, and the output is **bitwise equal** to the current kernel.

Related:
- #61996 / #54651 add the split pipeline for top-p-only rows; this PR covers rows with an active top-k.
- #595

items.summary: Fixes BlockObjectStoreError in MoE routing by retaining routed-expert outputs in auxiliary KV cache tiers so prefix hits don't serve blocks whose experts were evicted.
items.body:
## Purpose

Split from #58328, after #62392 and #62489.

- **Hit capping:** a local hit past the retained blocks is dropped. An external hit is trimmed to what the connector can load (new `KVConnectorBase_V1.external_load_alignment`, full attention only), or dropped if it loads only whole

[Perf] DSv4.1: Cache image preprocessing across requests

Multi-turn agents resend every earlier image on each turn, and the DeepSeek-V4.1 processor decodes and patchifies all of them again in the tokenizer process. This PR wires DeepSeek-V4.1 into it.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Adds env var SGLANG_BATCH_TOKENIZER_OUTPUTS to disable grouped IPC sends in detokenizer, reducing per-chunk latency for streaming workloads.

#44288 made the detokenizer group its return IPC sends by tokenizer worker: a batch of N requests spread over W workers now costs W sends instead of N. That is the right default for throughput serving.

items.title: [Perf] deepseek-v4.1: Skip the request-window history check when invariant checks are off
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: The predicate was built before the call, so its three kernels ran on every SWA layer even with off, the default. It has no recovery action, so nothing changes at any level except the skipped launches when it is off.
items.body:
- `RequestWindow.buffer` checks each SWA layer's history through `expect(_SWA_HISTORY_PRESENT, ...)` (#45223). The predicate `(tags[layer, src] == history_pos) | ~history_valid` was built before the call, so its three kernels ran on every SWA layer even with `SGLANG_INVARIANT_CHECK` off, the default.
- The check now runs only at WARN or above, the same gate other signal-only `expect` call sites use (`unified_hybrid_swa.py`, `dspark_planner.py`). It has no recovery action, so nothing changes at any level except the skipped launches when it is off.
- Verification:
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB30

items.author: hnyls2002

They run once per prefill step with encoder SWA replay on.

items.title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Drop deferred notifications for evicted remote engines
items.author: shubham-chakrawar3105
items.summary: Fixes KVConnector leaking pending notification entries for evicted remote engines, causing send failures or 60s libfabric connect stalls in P/D disaggregation.
items.body:
## Purpose

In P/D disaggregation with NixlConnector, a remote engine is evicted once it
sits idle past its TTL (engine_ttl). Eviction calls remove_remote_agent for
each of that engine's NIXL agents, but the deferred receive-notification map
(_pending_recv_notifs) is keyed by request id and keeps the removed agent
names. The next get_finished then calls _send_pending_recv_notifs, which sends
to an agent that eviction already removed. On UCX this fails; on the nixl 1.4
libfabric backend it blocks in connect() for up to 60s, the engine-starvation
path reported in #62144.

Partially addresses #62

items.title: [MoE] Add uniform subset MoE routing
items.author: askliar
items.summary: Add to the MoE routing simulator. This mode limits random routing to a configured expert prefix.
items.body:
## Overview

Add `uniform_subset` to the MoE routing simulator. This mode limits random routing to a configured expert prefix.

```text
uniform_subset
  read subset_size
  validate top_k <= subset_size <= num_experts
  select top_k distinct experts from [0, subset_size)
  assign weight 1.0 to each selected expert
```

## Claims

- Adds the `uniform_subset` routing strategy.
- Adds `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_SUBSET_SIZE`.
- Selects experts uniformly without replacement from `[0, subset_size)`.
- Rejects missing or invalid subset settings.
- Keeps the default routing path unchanged.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Fixes ledger drift in unified radix cache by decoupling logical token length from reclaimable pool length, preventing over-reporting during eviction and admission.
items.body:
## Motivation

A tree node's device value has two lengths that the tree cores treated as one: the logical length of the stored index tensor, which slicing, prefix matching and `collect_path_info` spans read, and the number of allocator slots the pool gets back when the value is evicted, which the evictable/protected ledgers count. A component whose backing is released or shared under a value can occupy fewer pool rows than the logical value describes, and the ledgers then drift from what the allocator actually reclaims: prefill admission adds the evictable ledger to the allocator's free space

items.title: [Perf] dspark: Make the prefill SWA valid-from update sync-free
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Replaces blocking pageable H2D copies and Python-list tensor indexing in DSpark prefill with async pinned transfers and device-side index_select, eliminating scheduler stalls and improving throughput by ~9%.
items.body:
- After a target prefill with encoder SWA replay, `DSparkWorkerV2._forward_prefill` marks each newly placed request's draft SWA ring valid from its cached prefix. It built the slots by indexing a CUDA tensor with a Python list and the prefix lengths with `torch.tensor(..., device=...)`. Both are pageable host-to-device copies that block the host. They run after the target forward is enqueued, so each prefill step stalled the scheduler until the whole target forward finished.
- Both copies now go through `async_h2d` (pinned, non-blocking), and the slots come from an `index_select` on the device

## Motivation

Pausing a dLLM server with `/pause_generation` in `retract` mode kills the scheduler. The next fetch then finds them twice and raises `Redundant requests detected in dLLM requests.` Requests that were waiting between blocks are not retracted at all, so they keep KV computed with the old weights, which defeats the purpose of a retracting pause during weight updates.

items.title: [Perf] unified-memory: Allocate free pages from each sub-pool's own end first
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: The unified memory pool shares one buffer between sub-pools that grow toward each other from its two ends (for example SWA from the low end and FULL from the high end). When a sub-pool reused freed pages, drained in list order for both grow directions.
items.body:
## Motivation

The unified memory pool shares one buffer between sub-pools that grow toward each other from its two ends (for example SWA from the low end and FULL from the high end). When a sub-pool reused freed pages, `MultiEndedAllocator.take_physical` drained `_free_phys_pages[:n]` in list order for both grow directions. Compaction sorts that list ascending and frees append to it unsorted, so a grow-down pool handed out its lowest free pages first: the ones nearest the boundary it shares with its neighbour rather than the ones nearest its own end. Fixes the DSpark speculative-decoding output corruption reported in #62417 (and any other model where a prefill-bearing batch can land in a FULL cudagraph).

Under `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, MRV2's varlen decode graphs are captured on a decode-shaped batch (num_reqs x 1 token per request, bucketed by padded token count). items.title: [Perf] qknorm: run head_dim-128 rows two per warp with 16B lanes, bit-identical
items.author: Monishver11
items.summary: In short: is the default QK-norm for Qwen3 dense and Qwen3-MoE on CUDA. At headdim 128 it gives each warp one (token, head) row, so a lane moves only 8 B per row.
items.body:
## Motivation

In short: `fused_qknorm_warp` is the default QK-norm for Qwen3 dense and Qwen3-MoE on CUDA. At head_dim 128 it gives each warp one (token, head) row, so a lane moves only 8 B per row. This PR runs two rows per warp with 16 B lanes, the same scheme mickqian merged for the diffusion QK-norm + RoPE kernel. The output is bit-identical. On an H100 NVL the kernel is 1.09-1.45x faster from 32 tokens up, and 1.29x inside a Qwen3-8B prefill trace; serving throughput is flat because the kernel is under 1% of GPU time.

items.body:
## Motivation

bdc1acf6cd (#2761, 2025-01-07) moved the first bucket of `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds` from 0.001 s to 0.1 s and stretched the tail from 30 s to 160 s, without saying why. Since then a short prompt on a current GPU, which gets its first token in tens of milliseconds, always lands in the first bucket, and the histogram can't tell 20 ms from 90 ms. The inter-token histogram starts at 0.002 s, and the sample output in `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx` still shows the `le="0.01"` to `le="0.08"` buckets.

Measured on 2026-10-17 with SGLang v0.5.21 serving Qwen3-8B

Large multi-image requests can block the tokenizer event loop while preparing a message for the scheduler when multimodal features travel inline as CPU tensors (`nnodes > 1`, or fallback after SHM allocation fails).

`get_new_expanded_mm_items()` splits a batched feature tensor into per-image views. A view can be contiguous while still retaining the entire batch's storage. PyTorch's pickle reducer serializes that storage for each distinct view, so the payload grows quadratically with the number of images.

For 96 images at 1024 x 1024, the processed float32 features occupy 2.25

items.title: [Fix] humming: Free replaced MoE weights after each sublayer transform
items.author: DarkraiHL
items.summary: replaces every MoE sublayer tensor with a padded, repacked copy of a different size while loading. The originals stay referenced until the next sublayer, and later allocations split their cached blocks, so much of that memory is never returned.
items.body:
## Motivation

`--moe-runner-backend humming` replaces every MoE sublayer tensor with a padded, repacked copy of a different size while loading. Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the scheduler-side hash fix. The store eviction fix is #62392.

`--kt-num-gpu-experts 0` keeps every routed expert on the CPU. `KTEPWrapperMethod.apply` still calls the GPU method with the masked dispatch, which then holds zero experts. items.title: [Feat] diffusion/minimax-h3: Add an online FP8 video VAE decoder
items.author: triple-mu
items.summary: Adds online FP8 W8A8 quantization to MiniMax-H3 video VAE decoder, reducing decode time by 40% with dynamic per-token activation scales.
items.body:
## Motivation

The MiniMax-H3 video VAE decode is dominated by its 36 ViT decoder blocks: 144 FP16 linears (`attn.to_qkv`, `attn.to_out`, `ff.w1`, `ff.w2`) run over every tile of every window, and there is no quantized checkpoint for the VAE. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 the decode stage takes 3.26 s of a 30 s five-step 768p request.

This PR converts those 144 linears to W8A8 FP8 once at load behind `--component-quantizations.video_vae fp8`: per-output-channel weight scales, dynamic per-token activation scales and the shared `apply_fp8_linear` dispatch, the recipe the DiT's online `--quantization fp8`

## Motivation

MiniMax-H3's video VAE decodes a request as overlapping spatial tiles over temporal windows and blends them back together. items.author: ZebornDuan
items.summary: V4 spreads KV, indexer, RoPE, and compressed state across multiple pools with different page sizes and layer mappings. Plain MLA dedup is not enough to restore all content, and allocating per pool separately would double-charge the same host budget.
items.body:
> Part of the HiCache MLA host-dedup series (see umbrella #45177). This is `[5/N]`. Depends on `[4/N]` (#45168 — `file` L3 for broadcast-mode dedup), which stacks on `[3/N]` (#45141 — L2 dedup **and** the shared-CPU-read path), `[2/N]` (#43798), and `[1/N]` (#43795). The shared-CPU-read extension for V4 is delivered in #45177.

## Motivation

V4 spreads KV, indexer, RoPE, and compressed state across multiple pools with different page sizes and layer mappings. Plain MLA dedup is not enough to restore all content, and allocating per pool separately would double-charge the same host budget.

…he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Zero out-of-window V in ROCM_ATTN's sliding-window kernels
items.author: zhentaocc
items.summary: Fixes NaN/Inf output in ROCm sliding-window attention by zeroing V for out-of-window KV cache slots in Triton kernels.
items.body:
## Overview

`ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton kernels (`context_attention_fwd` in `prefix_prefill.py` and `kernel_paged_attention_2d` in `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py`) mask QK for keys outside the sliding window but still load V for those keys unmasked. If an out-of-window slot sits in a freed block that now holds NaN/Inf, the output row becomes NaN even though its softmax weight is 0. This PR zeroes V for out-of-window tokens in both kernels.

items.title: [Bugfix] Floor the M-RoPE cache on the served window
items.author: wtogami
items.summary: Fixes a regression in v0.32 where M-RoPE cos/sin cache is undersized for models with length-extension rope scaling, causing out-of-bounds reads and crashes during inference.
items.body:
# [Bugfix] Floor the M-RoPE cache on the served window

Fixes #62383. This was a regression introduced in v0.32 where the engine can crash with Qwen 3.8 Flash Next.

## TL;DR

For scaling rope types (`yarn`/`longrope`), `get_rope()` builds the rope instance with
**`original_max_position_embeddings`** — the *pre-scaling* window — while served
positions still reach the full window (`max_model_len` = original × factor).
`MRotaryEmbedding` then allocated `base × 4` rows unconditionally, which silently
covered the gap for any scaling factor ≤ 4. #59853 correctly made that headroom
condit

items.author: samsja
items.summary: Fixes MXFP8 MoE decode producing garbage tokens after reload_weights by keeping the startup kernel and refreshing its quant config in place instead of rebuilding it.
items.body:
## Overview

Online MXFP8 MoE (`quantization="mxfp8"`) builds a new MoE kernel on every `reload_weights`, while decode keeps replaying CUDA graphs captured against the startup kernel. After the first reload, decode reads tensors freed with the old kernel and samples sporadic garbage tokens. This keeps the startup kernel on reload and refreshes its quant config in place.

Same class of bug as #61304 (ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE, behind `VLLM_RELOAD_KEEP_MOE_KERNEL`), which uses the same in-place refresh.

## Claims

- After `reload_weights`, online MXFP8 MoE decode with CUDA graphs matches eager prefi

Kimi-K3 stores vision-attention implementations in an `nn.ModuleDict`.
Previously, attention implementation labels were used directly as PyTorch

PyTorch rejects the child registration with:

## Motivation

The Mooncake direct linker loads an L3 hit with one synchronous `batch_get_into_multi_buffer_ranges` call per layer per pool, on a single thread. Each ranged op costs roughly 3 us serialized, so a DSA page-layer (a 72 KB KV range plus an 8 KB indexer range) moves at about 12-14 GB/s per rank, well below the NIC line rate. With a short new suffix on a long cached prefix (the common multi-turn / agentic shape) the load cannot hide behind compute, so it is directly on TTFT.

MLA context attention with chunked prefill (`MLA.forward_context_with_chunked_prefill` and `forward_context_with_cached_kv` in `tensorrt_llm/_torch/attention/mla.py`) builds the FMHA K for every cached-KV loop and for the current chunk as `maybe_compiled_cat((k_nope, k_pe.expand(-1, H, -1)), -1)` after a `split` and two `view`s. With batch-invariant inference and MLA latent caching enabled, a new request entering prefill can change the generated log-probabilities of requests already decoding. ### What does this PR do?

Optionally preserve in-flight vLLM requests across weight updates using native `pause_generation(mode="keep", clear_cache=False)`. Requests retain KV cache, generated tokens, logprobs and MoE routing, then resume without re-prefilling their history.

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

A DFlash drafter scores tokens through the target's `lm_head`. @coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fixes a server crash under speculative decoding with xgrammar guided decoding, and follows up on #20463.

**Crash.** Models pad the LM head past the tokenizer's vocabulary; Muse Spark Open has 201,818 tokens and 202,048 LM-head rows. `XGrammarMatcherFactory` gives xgrammar the padded size, and xgrammar's `TokenizerInfo` lists the extra ids as special tokens but keeps no decoded string for them. Asked to accept one, xgrammar before 0.2.6 (TRT-LLM pins 0.1.32) rejects it, but first prints its decoded string: an out-of-bounds read that segfaults the process.

Fixes #20485

## Description

This PR fixes two logic defects in `NGramPoolManager.get_draft_tokens`:

1. **Candidate pruning:** Removing elements from an `OrderedSet` while iterating over it can skip candidates, leaving shorter matches in the pool. Iterating over a snapshot (`list(pool[pattern])`) ensures all shorter matches are considered for removal.
2. **Single-match invariant:** When `is_keep_all=False`, the existing update branch can allow additional matches to be added to the pool. Guarding that branch with `self.is_keep_all` preserves the single-match behavior.

items.title: Fix padding-token zeroing for quantized inference under CUDA graphs
items.author: ilml
items.summary: Makes padding-token zeroing in dynamic inference work inside local CUDA graphs. Today it is skipped on every replay, so with FP8/FP4 the padding rows reach the per-tensor amax with whatever stale memory they hold.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Makes padding-token zeroing in dynamic inference work inside local CUDA graphs. Today it is skipped on every replay, so with FP8/FP4 the padding rows reach the per-tensor amax with whatever stale memory they hold.

This is why `gpt_dynamic_inference_tp1_pp1_583m_cuda_graphs_fp8_logitsmatch` (GitLab, H100) has failed on every `main` pipeline since 2026-09-17, always with the same output: token 5 diverges from the golden.

## Root cause

#2585 added the zeroing to keep padding tokens out of FP8 amax

items.title: [MoE] Opt-in EP-size-invariant expert combine (fixed fp32 reduction tree)
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout.
items.body:
**Problem.** Under `batch_invariant_mode`, the MoE combine sums each token's local expert outputs per EP rank, rounds that partial to fp32, and then adds the rank partials in rank order. Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout. That rules out, for example, training at EP8 while generating at EP4.

Measured on Nemotron-3-Nano (top-6, hidden 2688) in our RL setup, which uses the same combine:
- One MoE layer at EP2 vs EP1

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.title: Fix FP8/FP4 context loss during GDN and KDA recompute
items.author: QiZhangNV
items.summary: When selective recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward.
items.body:
When selective `gdn` recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward. With MXFP8 parameter gathering enabled, this can also cause a missing `main_grad` error.

Use `te_checkpoint` for FP8/FP4 in GDN and KDA to preserve the quantization context, keeping the existing checkpoint path for non-quantized configurations.

Validated with 12 GPU regression cases and a single-node, four-GPU Qwen-style proxy covering MXFP8, NVFP4, and MXFP8 parameter gathering.

items.summary: With, budgets each micro-batch by the sum of its real tokens. On the Megatron BSHD path, however, every micro-batch is stored as tokens: it is padded to its longest sequence (or to the mini-batch max with ) and then aligned for TP/CP/FP8.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

## 背景

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。

此工作流在 `verl-project/verl` 仓库中运行，并使用**独立的私有 Fork 仓库**来存储翻译工具（Python 翻译引擎、技能/提示文档以及 `.po` 翻译记忆库）。这使得上游仓库保持整洁——它仅接收 `en/` 文档和工作流文件的更改。

1. **检出（Checkout）** Fork 私有仓库的 `main` 分支（包含 `translate_md.py`、`skill.md`、`.po` 缓存）。
2. **同步（Sync）** Fork 的 `main` 分支与最新的上游 `main` 分支（通过 `git merge`），然后将同步后的 `main` 分支推送回 Fork。
3. **翻译（Translate）** — 运行 `translate_md.py`，将每个中文文档拆分为块，复用 `.po` 文件中的缓存翻译，仅对更改/未翻译的块调用 OpenAI 兼容的

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. A `BaseTool` therefore cannot keep state from one turn to the next, although `BaseTool.create` is documented as creating "a tool instance for a trajectory" and `docs/sglang_multiturn/multiturn.rst` points to `BaseTool` for per-trajectory state such as sandbox VMs, scratch directories and DB rows.

This PR creates the instance on the first call to a tool, reuses it for the rest of the trajectory, and releases every instance once when the trajectory ends, including when it raises.

items.author: kahlun
items.summary: pins this rank's accelerator only when a variable is set. In the default configuration verl never calls at all, and instead relies on Ray's per-actor visibility mask relabeling devices so that index 0 is this rank's device.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`Worker._setup_env_cuda_visible_devices()` pins this rank's accelerator only when a
`RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_*_VISIBLE_DEVICES` variable is set. In the default configuration verl
never calls `set_device()` at all, and instead relies on Ray's per-actor visibility mask
relabeling devices so that index 0 is this rank's device.

That assumption holds only where the accelerator runtime honors its own visibility mask. Where
it does not, every rank in the job runs on the same physical device. The collision does not
raise a device error — it surfaces as out-of-memory

items.summary: The previous condition also selects that substitute for a PEFT module whose MRO puts before. Its class swap then fails with.
items.body:
## Problem

FSDP2 temporarily substitutes `FSDPModule` while wrapping an `ABC`-first
`nn.Module`. The previous `isinstance(model, ABC)` condition also selects that
substitute for a PEFT module whose MRO puts `nn.Module` before `ABC`. Its class
swap then fails with `TypeError: __class__ assignment: object layout differs`.

## Change

Choose the substitute only when `ABC` actually precedes `nn.Module` in the
module's MRO. The existing behavior for `ABC`-first modules is unchanged.

## Scope and duplicate check

This is a training-side FSDP2 class-layout fix. It does not implement a model
adapter

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8076. Setting `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.dtype=float16` currently leaves FSDP compute and autocast in BF16 when `mixed_precision.param_dtype` is absent, so the FP16 gradient scaler is also omitted.

Use the engine's `dtype` as the default for both an absent and a partial `mixed_precision` mapping. Explicit `param_dtype` overrides still take precedence; reduction and buffer defaults remain FP32. The existing wrapper, autocast and scaler setup then receives the configured dtype.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

The startup path previously selected one set of returned IDs without checking that:

items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups. Explicit ABORTED retries and intentional shutdown cancellation keep their existing behavior.

Closes https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/2399

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.author: YeonwooSung
items.summary: used to center, scale, then add the mean back: That is not a scale-only path. This change makes do what it says: - (default): — zero-mean, unit-variance -: — scale only; do not subtract the mean, and do not add it back Both paths still share the same Bessel-co…

Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

```
whitened_values = (values - global_mean) * rsqrt(var)
if not shift_mean:
    whitened_values += global_mean
```

items.title: fix: cancel pending rollout tasks after a failure
items.author: yuyz-cyber
items.summary: When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task except…
items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

When `--use-kl-loss` is enabled with `kl_loss_coef == 0`, slime still
constructs the reference KL autograd graph and adds the following term to the

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

items.body:
`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.

## Problem

`pytest-utils-tests` CI job (bare `python:3.11`, no GPU vllm) fails at collection:

```
tests/utils/test_vllm_engine.py:21: from vime.backends.vllm_utils import vllm_engine as mod

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm.utils.system_utils'; 'vllm.utils' is not a package
```

`install_vllm_cli_stubs()` registered `vllm.utils` as a plain `ModuleType` (no `__path__`), so importing any submodule of it failed.

items.title: fix(examples/tau-bench): use RunConfig.agent_strategy in TAU_CONFIGS (slime #2101)
items.author: CalvinXKY
items.summary: tau-bench's defines, not. The previous key was silently ignored by Pydantic, so changing the agent type in had no effect (the default was always used).
items.body:
## Summary

- Fix `TAU_CONFIGS` in the tau-bench example to use `agent_strategy` instead of `agent`.
- Update the README snippet to match.

tau-bench's `RunConfig` defines `agent_strategy`, not `agent`. The previous key was silently ignored by Pydantic, so changing the agent type in `TAU_CONFIGS` had no effect (the default `tool-calling` was always used). `resolve_tau_config()` also accessed `tau_config.agent`, which raises `AttributeError` at rollout time.

Same fix as THUDM/slime#2101.

## Test plan

- [x] `RunConfig(**TAU_CONFIGS)` accepts the config without extra/ignored fields
- [x] Setti
